facts.raw_span: A 53-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (>30 years)
presented with weakness, bloating, anorexia, and decreased urine output for 10 days
denied any history of infectious disease, such as typhoid or tuberculosis, chronic disease, such as hypertension or diabetes, or recent surgery or trauma
Blood pressure on admission was 153/89 mmHg
developed fever (39°C) with obvious tenderness of the left lumbar vertebra
temperature increased to 40.2°C, accompanied by chills, severe low back pain, and forced position
ALT: 160 U/L (ref: 0-40)
AST: 167 U/L (ref: 0-40)
Abdominal ultrasound showed liver cirrhosis and ascites with maximum anteroposterior diameter of 132 mm
Blood culture positive with grayish white colonies on blood agar and green colonies on TCBS agar
16S rRNA sequencing confirmed organism identity
Antibiotic susceptibility testing showed sensitivity to multiple antibiotics
